clue.text: Cooking in a dream, one might put chicken in this

definitions.text: one might put chicken in this

indicators.note: cooking up something means concocting it, so these letters are mixed into a new order

parts.note: the fodder, taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: A cook drifts off and imagines putting a chicken into a pot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cooking' looks like part of the kitchen scene but it is the anagram signal working on IN A DREAM.
explanation.definitionFit: A marinade is a seasoned liquid in which meat such as chicken is soaked before cooking.

clue.text: Very quick power nap, perhaps, then nothing

parts.note: P is the physics symbol for power
a nap is an example of a rest
O, the figure zero, is nothing

explanation.surface: A burst of energy followed by a quick snooze, then nothing at all.
explanation.definitionFit: The musical direction tells players to perform at a very fast tempo, so it means very quick.

clue.text: Funniness about a delay

indicators.note: the word for funniness goes about, that is around, the letter A

parts.note: wit is cleverness that makes people laugh

explanation.surface: Something amusing concerning a hold-up.
explanation.definitionFit: To wait is to hold back or stay put, a synonym of delay as a verb.

clue.text: Cut short revolutionary phrase that's overused

indicators.note: cut short: the word loses its last letter

parts.note: to clip is to cut
Che Guevara, the Argentine Marxist revolutionary

explanation.surface: An instruction to trim a worn-out revolutionary slogan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' trims CLIP to CLI; Che Guevara supplies the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: A cliche is a stock expression worn out from too much repetition.

clue.text: Traitor making arrangement to cede fort

indicators.note: making an arrangement of letters means putting them in a new order

parts.note: the fodder, taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: A turncoat arranges to hand over a stronghold to the enemy.
explanation.definitionFit: A defector abandons their own side for the enemy, which is a kind of betrayal.

clue.text: Drive round Northern Ireland is fine, perhaps

indicators.note: the word for drive goes round the abbreviation

parts.note: to push is to drive or urge forward

explanation.surface: Reads like a comment that a drive round Northern Ireland is a fine idea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fine' looks like an adjective meaning good, but here it is the verb: to impose a monetary penalty.
explanation.definitionFit: Fining someone is one way of penalising them, so it is an example of the answer.

clue.text: Ends up in a narrow tongue of land

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: tips are ends, as of fingers

explanation.surface: Describes where something finishes: on a thin strip of land.
explanation.definitionFit: A spit is a long narrow point of sand or shingle running out into the sea.

clue.text: Trouble about girl's high-flown writings?

indicators.note: the word for trouble goes about, around, the girl's name

parts.note: to ail is to trouble or afflict
Irma is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A worry over a young woman's pretentious prose.
explanation.walkthrough: 'High-flown' usually means pompous; the question mark signals the literal sense, letters flown high by plane.
explanation.definitionFit: Letters sent by aeroplane literally travel high in the sky, a playful reading of lofty correspondence.

clue.text: Supply English joke

parts.note: a quip is a witty remark or joke

explanation.surface: Provide a typically English witticism.
explanation.definitionFit: To equip someone is to furnish or provide them with what they need.

clue.text: Something implanted inside group

parts.note: in means inside
a set is a group of things

explanation.surface: Describes an object embedded within a cluster.
explanation.definitionFit: An inset is a piece set into a larger thing, such as a panel or small map placed within another.

clue.text: Scientist's note found in box

indicators.note: the note is found placed in the box word

parts.note: a chest is a large box
mi is the third note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A researcher's memo is discovered inside a container.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is read as 'is', linking the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A chemist is a scientist who studies the substances matter is made of.

clue.text: A point about Royal Navy chaps showing tattoo, perhaps

indicators.note: the word for point goes about, around, the navy and chaps

parts.note: a dot is a small point
chaps are men

explanation.surface: Sailors with a tattoo, a classic naval image, centred on a single point.
explanation.definitionFit: A tattoo can be worn as decoration of the body, making it an example of an ornament.

clue.text: Snubs men developing a lack of feeling

indicators.note: developing suggests the letters grow into a new form, so they are rearranged

parts.note: the fodder, taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: Someone who ignores men may be growing emotionally cold.
explanation.definitionFit: Numbness is the loss of sensation, physical or emotional, so a lack of feeling.

clue.text: It is associated with hotel buffet

parts.note: H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Suggests a hotel known for its buffet meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'buffet' looks like a spread of food, but it is the verb meaning to strike.
explanation.definitionFit: To buffet is to strike repeatedly, so a hit is a synonym in the sense of a blow.

clue.text: Time to allay the fear of losing son and wealth

indicators.note: the word for comforting someone is losing one letter

parts.note: to reassure someone is to allay their fear

explanation.surface: Suggests it takes time to calm a parent worried about losing their son and fortune.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of losing' takes one S out of REASSURE to leave REASURE.
explanation.definitionFit: Treasure is accumulated riches such as gold and jewels, so it means wealth.

clue.text: Part of another age or epoch

indicators.note: the answer is a part of the run of letters in these words

explanation.surface: Reads like a phrase from a history book: part of another period or time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'age' looks like part of the definition, but it supplies the A of the hidden word.
explanation.definitionFit: An era is a long period of history, a synonym of epoch.

clue.text: A small seabird at the back of the ship

definitions.text: at the back of the ship

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
a tern is a slender seabird

explanation.surface: A little seabird perches at the stern of a vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: The nautical term describes the position behind or towards the rear of a vessel.

clue.text: Rebels' aim in revolution is causing unhappiness

indicators.note: letters in revolution are overturned and rearranged

parts.note: the fodder, taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: Insurgents' goal of uprising brings sorrow.
explanation.definitionFit: Something miserable makes people wretched, so it brings about sorrow.

clue.text: Outline of second sailing boat

parts.note: a ketch is a two-masted sailing boat

explanation.surface: A rough drawing of a second sailing boat.
explanation.definitionFit: A sketch is a rough drawing or brief description, giving the main points only.

clue.text: Burial place of old British missile

parts.note: an arrow is a missile shot from a bow

explanation.surface: An ancient British burial mound with a weapon inside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'old British' reads as a phrase, but 'old' belongs to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A barrow is an ancient mound of earth raised over a grave, a prehistoric tomb.

clue.text: At home, with friend round before start of early afternoon show

indicators.note: the word for friend goes round the word for at home

parts.note: a mate is a friend
in means at home

indicators.note: only the first letter of the word is used

explanation.surface: Staying in with a pal before heading to an early afternoon performance.
explanation.definitionFit: A matinee is a performance at a theatre or cinema held during the daytime.

clue.text: Male at top of excellent club

parts.note: ace is slang for excellent

explanation.surface: A man at the head of a first-rate club.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at top of' puts the M first in this down answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A mace is a heavy club with a spiked head, used as a weapon.

clue.text: Initially very ill, really unwell … suffering this?

definitions.text: Initially very ill, really unwell … suffering this?

indicators.note: initially means the first letter of each following word is taken

explanation.surface: Someone who is feeling very poorly asks what infection they might have.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: the initials spell the answer, and the clue describes what makes one so ill.
explanation.definitionFit: A virus is an infectious agent that makes someone feel very ill when they catch it.

clue.text: Very last market

parts.note: the end is the last part

explanation.surface: Describes the very final market of the season.
explanation.walkthrough: 'market' looks like a noun but is the verb meaning to sell.
explanation.definitionFit: To vend is to sell goods, and to market something is to offer it for sale.

clue.text: Pack of scoundrels surrounding king

indicators.note: the word for scoundrels goes around the king's letter

parts.note: cads are scoundrels, dishonourable men
R, from Latin rex, is the abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A gang of rogues closes in around a monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pack of' looks like a collective noun for the scoundrels; 'Pack' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A pack is a full set of playing cards used for games.

clue.text: Clubs travelling round line shown on map

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for clubs, the card suit
a band travelling round the country is on tour

explanation.surface: Golf clubs being carried around on a trip, mapped as they go.
explanation.definitionFit: A contour is a line on a map joining points of equal height above sea level.
